'''David J. Lipman''' is an American [[biologist]] who from 1989<ref name=LipmanDirNCBI.NYT>{{cite news
      |newspaper=[[The New York Times]]
      |title=Research Institute Posts Gene Data on Internet
      |url=http://www.nytimes.com/library/cyber/week/062697gene.html
      |date=June 26, 1997}}</ref> to 2017 was the director of the [[National Center for Biotechnology Information]] (NCBI) at the [[National Institutes of Health]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/staff/lipman/ |title=David J. Lipman, MD, Director, National Center for Biotechnology Information |archive-date=2013-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926162806/http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/staff/lipman/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biomedcentral.com/openaccess/archive/?page=features&issue=2 |title=Open Access Now &#124; Conversation with David Lipman |website=Biomedcentral.com |access-date=2 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629170212/http://www.biomedcentral.com/openaccess/archive/?page=features&issue=2 |archive-date=29 June 2011 }}</ref> NCBI is the home of [[GenBank]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Benson | first1 = D. A. | last2 = Karsch-Mizrachi | first2 = I. | last3 = Lipman | first3 = D. J. | last4 = Ostell | first4 = J. | last5 = Wheeler | first5 = D. L. | title = GenBank | doi = 10.1093/nar/gkm929 | journal = Nucleic Acids Research | volume = 36 | issue = Database issue | pages = D25–D30 | year = 2007 | pmid =  18073190| pmc =2238942 }}</ref> the U.S. node of the [[INSDC|International Sequence Database Consortium]], and [[PubMed]], one of the most heavily used sites in the world for the search and retrieval of biomedical information. Lipman is one of the original authors of the [[BLAST (biotechnology)|BLAST]] sequence alignment program, and a respected figure in [[bioinformatics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=david+lipman |title=david lipman – Google Scholar |website=Scholar.google.com |access-date=2017-03-26}}</ref><ref name="dblp">{{DBLP|name=David J. Lipman}}</ref> In 2017, he left NCBI and became Chief Science Officer at [[Impossible Foods]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nlm.nih.gov/news/nlm_announces_departure_of_ncbi_director_david_lipman.html|title=National Library of Medicine Announces Departure of NCBI Director Dr. David Lipman|website=www.nlm.nih.gov|access-date=2017-05-05}}</ref>

==Education==
Lipman received his undergraduate degree from [[Brown University]] and his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] in 1980 from the [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York]]<ref>{{cite web|title=David J. Lipman, M.D. Biography|url=https://irp.nih.gov/pi/david-lipman|website=nih.gov|access-date=2017-02-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211080242/https://irp.nih.gov/pi/david-lipman|archive-date=2017-02-11|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
Lipman was the founding director of the [[National Center for Biotechnology Information]], part of the [[National Library of Medicine]] at the U.S. National Institutes of Health. Under his leadership, NCBI grew from fewer than a dozen people to more than 500 scientific staff, and it now hosts hundreds of scientific and medical databases including [[GenBank]], [[PubMed]], [[PubMed Central]], dbGaP, dbSNP, the Sequence Read Archive (SRA), RefSeq, PubChem, and many more. The internal research program at NCBI included groups led by [[Stephen Altschul]] (another BLAST co-author), David Landsman, [[Eugene Koonin]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Tatusov | first1 = R. L. | last2 = Koonin | first2 = E. V. | last3 = Lipman | first3 = D. J. | doi = 10.1126/science.278.5338.631 | title = A Genomic Perspective on Protein Families | journal = Science | volume = 278 | issue = 5338 | pages = 631–637 | year = 1997 | pmid =  9381173| url = https://zenodo.org/record/1231126 | bibcode = 1997Sci...278..631T }}</ref> (a prolific author on [[comparative genomics]]), and L. Aravind.

Lipman is very well known for his seminal work on a series of sequence similarity algorithms, starting from the Wilbur-Lipman<ref>{{Cite journal

BLAST eventually became the most widely used and highly cited (over 160,000 citations as of 2021) sequence alignment program in the field, and the NCBI BLAST server today is one of its most heavily used resources.

Lipman also worked for many years with Dennis A. Benson and others at NCBI on the maintenance and improvement of [[GenBank]], one of the world's largest databases of genome and protein sequence data. GenBank along with the [[European Nucleotide Archive]] and the [[DNA Data Bank of Japan]] form the [[International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration]] (INSDC), a fully open, unrestricted database of genome sequences that has been the world's repository of such data since 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal

He was one of the originators of the [[Influenza Genome Sequencing Project]], a project to sequence and make available the genomes of thousands of influenza virus isolates.{{citation needed|date=March 2017}}

He was one of the original signatories of the [[Bethesda Statement on Open Access Publishing]].{{citation needed|date=July 2020}}

He is also the [[editor-in-chief]] for an [[open access|open-access]], [[peer review|peer-reviewed]] online [[scientific journal]] called ''[[Biology Direct]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biology-direct.com/about/edboard |title=Biology Direct &#124; Editorial board |access-date=2011-10-28 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110930060756/http://www.biology-direct.com/about/edboard |archive-date=2011-09-30 }}</ref>

In May 2017, Lipman left his role at the NCBI to join the plant-based meat company [[Impossible Foods]] as chief scientific officer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nlm.nih.gov/news/nlm_announces_departure_of_ncbi_director_david_lipman.html|title=National Library of Medicine Announces Departure of NCBI Director Dr. David Lipman|website=www.nlm.nih.gov|access-date=2017-05-04}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Lipman received the [[Association of Biomolecular Resource Facilities]] Award for outstanding contributions to Biomolecular Technologies in 1996.

In 2000, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Medicine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/institute-medicine-elects-new-members |title=Institute of Medicine Elects New Members}}</ref>

In 2004, he was awarded the [[ISCB Senior Scientist Award]] and elected an [[ISCB Fellow]] in 2009 by the [[International Society for Computational Biology]].<ref name=fellows/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iscb.org/images/stories/newsletter/newsletter7-3/ssaa.html |title=ISCB Names 2004 Senior Scientist Accomplishment Award Winner, Dr. David Lipman ISCB Newsletter 7-3 |website=Iscb.org |access-date=2 July 2011}}</ref>

In 2005, Dr. Lipman was elected to the US [[National Academy of Sciences]].{{citation needed|date=March 2017}}

In 2013, he received the award of a [[White House]] "Open Science" Champion of Change.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/champions/open-science |title=Open Science &#124; the White House |access-date=2016-04-02 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170121053707/https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/champions/open-science |via=[[NARA|National Archives]] |work=[[whitehouse.gov]] |archive-date=2017-01-21 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/news/06-20-2013-whitehouse-champion-of-change-award/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705193953/http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/news/06-20-2013-whitehouse-champion-of-change-award/|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 5, 2013|title=Dr. David Lipman Receives White House "Open Science" Champions of Change Award on Behalf of NCBI|website=Ncbi.nlm.nih.gov|access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref>

In 2023, he was awarded the [[Warren Alpert Foundation Prize]].<ref>[https://warrenalpert.org/news/2023-warren-alpert-foundation-prize-recipient-announced Warren Alpert Foundation Prize 2023]</ref>
